title: Cascade Harness Radar — Dossier Section Contract (v1)
description: The canonical shape a synthesis agent must return when composing a HARNESS dossier or a BENCHMARK dossier from harvested evidence. A 'harness' is an AI coding agent / scaffold — the loop around a model that plans, edits files, runs tools, and iterates (e.g. OpenHands, Aider, SWE-agent, Cline, Goose, Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI, Cursor). This is the SIBLING contract to Model Radar's dossier-schema.json: same claim/stance/confidence/divergence machinery, same meta-rating + capability-vector idea, but the SUBJECT is the harness, not the model. Every claim-bearing entry carries a stance (whose kind of voice made the claim), source attribution, and a confidence ('low' | 'medium' | 'high'). SLUG RULES — harness_slug is the lowercase-hyphenated canonical harness slug (e.g. 'openhands', 'aider', 'claude-code', 'codex-cli', 'swe-agent'); family_slug groups related harnesses/editions of one project (e.g. 'openhands', 'copilot'); benchmark slugs are likewise lowercase-hyphenated (e.g. 'swe-bench-verified', 'terminal-bench', 'aider-polyglot'). FAMILY ROLLUP — a family is a QUERY-TIME grouping over harness dossiers sharing a family_slug; there is NO stored family object. BENCHMARK DOSSIERS ARE SHARED with Model Radar — one canonical benchmark_dossier per benchmark_slug, cited by both radars; Harness Radar stamps type_data.radar_scope to include 'harness' on any benchmark it touches so the /harnesses view can scope to harness-relevant benchmarks.

stance.description: Whose kind of voice a claim comes from. 'maker_claim' = the harness's own maker/vendor announcement, docs, README, or marketing (e.g. All Hands AI on OpenHands, Anthropic on Claude Code, Aider's own leaderboard). 'independent_eval' = third-party benchmark runs, structured evals, comparative reviews. 'practitioner_take' = hands-on builder/creator experience reports and opinions. Per-source stance hints in sources.json are DEFAULTS; extraction may override per evidence item (e.g. a practitioner video quoting a maker's benchmark table yields a maker_claim item).

confidence.description: Categorical confidence in a claim — the ONE confidence scale for this contract (three-level categorical; 0..1 numeric was considered and rejected for cross-agent consistency). 'high' = corroborated across stances or from a rigorous independent eval; 'medium' = single credible source or partially corroborated; 'low' = anecdotal, contested, or maker-only with no independent check.

slug.description: Lowercase-hyphenated canonical slug: lowercase letters, digits, hyphens, with dots permitted inside version tokens. Examples — harnesses: 'openhands', 'aider', 'claude-code', 'codex-cli', 'swe-agent', 'cline', 'goose'; families: 'openhands', 'copilot'; benchmarks: 'swe-bench-verified', 'terminal-bench', 'aider-polyglot'.

source_ref.description: Attribution for one piece of evidence backing a claim. url should be the normalized canonical URL (dedup-comparable, matching the /cse:ingest convention: lowercased host, utm_*/fbclid/gclid + fragment + trailing slash stripped).

url.description: Normalized canonical URL of the source.

author.description: Person or outlet behind the source (e.g. 'All Hands AI', 'Aider', 'SWE-bench team').

source_id.description: Optional id of the registry entry in sources.json this evidence was harvested from.

stance.description: Stance of THIS evidence item — may override the source's default stance_hint.

published_date.description: ISO date the source was published, if discoverable.

claim.description: One claim-bearing entry. Every claim carries its stance, its confidence ('low'|'medium'|'high'), and source attribution.

statement.description: Full standalone sentence carrying the specific detail/number/example from the evidence (not generic).

divergence_side.description: One side of a contested question: the position taken, which stances are on this side, and the sources arguing it.

position.description: The position this side takes, stated as a standalone sentence.

stances.description: Which stance(s) are on this side of the divergence (e.g. maker_claim on one side, practitioner_take on the other).

confidence.description: Confidence that this side's position is accurately represented by the cited sources.

divergence_entry.description: One contested question where credible sources disagree — the signal a single-stance summary would flatten. Each entry names the topic and lays out the opposing sides with position, stances, and attribution.

topic.description: What the disagreement is about (e.g. 'true autonomy vs. babysitting required on large repos').

assessment.description: Optional synthesis judgment: which side the evidence favors and why, or 'unresolved'.

axis_score.description: One scored HARNESS capability axis. 'axis' is one of the 6 core axis ids — 'agentic_capability', 'context_management', 'tool_integration', 'model_flexibility', 'control_safety', 'ecosystem_maturity' — or an emergent slug. RUBRIC — 'value' is an integer 0-100 scored RELATIVE to the current frontier of harnesses: 90-100 frontier-leading, 70-89 strong, 40-69 mid, <40 weak/unproven. The rationale is load-bearing: it MUST cite a specific score snapshot or evidence package, never vibes.

axis.description: Axis id: one of the 6 core ids ('agentic_capability', 'context_management', 'tool_integration', 'model_flexibility', 'control_safety', 'ecosystem_maturity') or an emergent slug.

value.description: 0-100 score relative to the current frontier: 90-100 frontier-leading, 70-89 strong, 40-69 mid, <40 weak/unproven.

rationale.description: Why this value — MUST cite a specific score snapshot or evidence package backing the number.

sources.description: Optional attribution for the evidence behind this axis score.

emergent_axis_score.description: An axis_score for an EMERGENT axis — a capability dimension the 6 core axes don't cover (e.g. 'token_efficiency', 'multimodal', 'cloud_autonomy'). Add one only when 2+ independent evidence items support the dimension; never duplicate a core axis. Same shape and rubric as axis_score, plus a REQUIRED 'definition'.

axis.description: Emergent axis slug (lowercase-hyphenated or snake_case id, distinct from all 6 core axis ids).

value.description: 0-100 score relative to the current frontier: 90-100 frontier-leading, 70-89 strong, 40-69 mid, <40 weak/unproven.

rationale.description: Why this value — MUST cite a specific score snapshot or evidence package backing the number.

definition.description: REQUIRED for emergent axes: what this axis measures and why the evidence (2+ independent items) supports adding it beyond the 6 core axes.

sources.description: Optional attribution for the evidence behind this axis score.

capability_vector.description: The structured capability profile of one harness: ALL 6 core axes scored (agentic_capability, context_management, tool_integration, model_flexibility, control_safety, ecosystem_maturity), plus any emergent axes the evidence supports. This shape is the canonical contract shared with score-schema.json and the TypeScript types — field names are load-bearing.

core.description: All 6 core axes scored — one axis_score per core axis id. minItems 6: a capability vector with a missing core axis is invalid; use 'insufficient_evidence' plus a low-confidence score rather than omitting an axis.

emergent.description: Optional emergent axes — only when 2+ independent evidence items support a dimension the core 6 don't cover (e.g. 'token_efficiency').

synthesized_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the synthesis run that produced this vector.

harness_slug.description: Optional canonical harness slug this vector describes (redundant with the enclosing dossier when embedded; useful when the vector travels alone, e.g. in package type_data).

insufficient_evidence.description: Honest statement when the evidence base is thin — which axes are under-evidenced and why the scores there should be read cautiously.

divergence_flag.description: Explicit honesty marker for one place where the NUMBERS and the DISCOURSE disagree — e.g. a harness tops SWE-bench Verified while practitioners report real-repo thrashing. Distinct from divergence_entry (source-vs-source disagreement): this flags structured-score-vs-narrative divergence.

topic.description: What the divergence is about (e.g. 'real-repo reliability').

discourse_says.description: What maker claims and/or practitioner discourse say.

axis.description: Optional axis id the divergence bears on (core id or emergent slug).

assessment.description: Researcher judgment on which side the evidence favors and why, or 'unresolved'.

sources.description: Optional attribution for the discourse side of the divergence.

meta_rating.description: Researcher-voice META-RATING of one harness, synthesized from the full stored score-snapshot series plus all discourse evidence. The narrative reads like an indiscriminate researcher writing a paper across the industry's coding-agent benchmarks — deducing what the numbers mean rather than repeating them — citing specific snapshots and discourse, and staying honest about insufficiency and about places where numbers and discourse disagree.

narrative.description: Researcher-voice meta-analysis: what the benchmark record and discourse, taken together, say this harness actually is. Cites specific score snapshots + discourse evidence; honest about insufficient evidence.

divergence_notes.description: Explicit honesty: every place the structured numbers and the discourse disagree.

updated_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp this meta-rating was last updated.

standing_entry.description: One harness's current standing on a benchmark — a single (harness, value, as-of) point derived from the stored score-snapshot series. model_slug records which underlying model produced the number (harness scores are combos).

harness_slug.description: Canonical harness slug holding this standing.

model_slug.description: Optional underlying model slug the harness ran to produce this number.

value.description: The score value as reported for this benchmark (in the benchmark's native metric/unit).

as_of.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) the score was reported/snapshot — the standing's freshness stamp.

metric.description: Optional metric name when the benchmark reports several (e.g. 'resolved_rate').

config.description: Optional scaffold/config caveat for the harness run (e.g. 'CodeAct v3', 'bash-only').

source_slug.description: Optional slug/id of the source or leaderboard the snapshot came from.

score_context.description: Current standings + score dynamics for one benchmark, derived from the append-only score_snapshots series stored in package type_data — grounded in stored snapshots, not vibes. For a HARNESS benchmark, standings list harnesses (harness_slug, optionally with the model they ran).

standings.description: Current top harnesses on this benchmark with as-of dates, derived from the stored snapshot series.

dynamics.description: Score dynamics over the stored series: movement, saturation, new entrants, scaffold-vs-model confound — grounded in stored snapshots, not vibes.

as_of.description: Optional ISO timestamp this context was derived.

harness_dossier.title: Harness Dossier
harness_dossier.description: Dossier for ONE canonical AI coding harness (one harness_slug). Family-level views ('how does the OpenHands line compare across editions?') are computed at query time by grouping dossiers on family_slug — no family object is ever stored.

harness_slug.description: Canonical harness slug, lowercase-hyphenated (e.g. 'openhands', 'aider', 'claude-code'). One dossier per harness — this is the dossier's identity key.

family_slug.description: Optional. Groups related harnesses/editions of one project (e.g. 'openhands' for OpenHands CLI + Cloud, 'copilot' for Copilot's chat + agent). Family rollup is a QUERY-TIME grouping by this field; no family object is stored.

maker.description: Who makes the harness (e.g. 'All Hands AI', 'Aider / Paul Gauthier', 'Anthropic', 'OpenAI', 'Princeton NLP', 'Cline Bot Inc.').

open_source.description: Whether the harness is open source (source-available under an OSI-ish license the user can run/modify). The core Harness Radar distinction — open-source harnesses are the ones users can actually play with inside Cascade.

license.description: License string when known (e.g. 'MIT', 'Apache-2.0', 'AGPL-3.0', 'proprietary'). Absent/unknown → omit.

repo_url.description: Canonical source repository URL for open-source harnesses (e.g. GitHub), when it exists.

surfaces.description: Which surfaces the harness ships (e.g. ['cli'] for Aider, ['cli','ide','cloud'] for a broad harness). Empty/unknown → omit.

first_release.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) the harness first shipped publicly, or the literal 'unknown' when the evidence never states it — never fabricate.

last_synthesized_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent synthesis run that produced/updated this dossier.

superseded_by.description: Optional. harness_slug of the harness that supersedes/replaces this one (e.g. a dossier for 'opendevin' pointing at 'openhands' after the rename/rebrand). Absent while the harness is current.

strengths.description: What the harness is demonstrably good at. Each entry is a claim with stance, confidence, and sources.

risks.description: Weaknesses, failure modes, safety/cost/reliability concerns, lock-in. Each entry is a claim with stance, confidence, and sources.

post_release_findings.description: Field findings — what emerged from real-world use after launch: independent benchmark runs landing, practitioner experience accumulating, quiet capability discoveries, reliability/cost reports. This is where the dossier diverges from the launch-day pitch. Each entry is a claim with stance, confidence, and sources.

divergence.description: Contested questions where sources DISAGREE — each entry carries the opposing positions, which stances sit on each side, and attribution. Preserving disagreement (rather than averaging it away) is the point of this section.

fit_for_our_stack.description: How this harness fits OUR stack — notes grounded in org context (for Cascade HQ: Max Plan vs API billing, MCP tooling, the interactive-terminal + PWA workflow, the Supabase/Next.js codebase, whether it can drive the cse plugin's skills). This section is org-specific by design and is synthesized against .cascade/context/ and org memory, not just public evidence.

summary.description: 2-4 sentence bottom line: adopt / trial / watch / skip for our stack, and why.

considerations.description: Specific fit notes (model/plan fit — e.g. does it run on Max Plan OAuth or force an API key; MCP support; integration surface; migration cost; workflow impact). Each is a claim with stance, confidence, and sources.

meta_rating.description: OPTIONAL. Researcher-voice META-RATING synthesized from the full score-snapshot series plus all discourse evidence. Persisted BOTH here (artifact body) and structured on the package row as type_data.capability_vector.

benchmark_dossier.title: Benchmark Dossier
benchmark_dossier.description: Dossier for ONE benchmark (one benchmark_slug, lowercase-hyphenated, e.g. 'swe-bench-verified', 'terminal-bench', 'aider-polyglot'). Captures what it tests, whether to trust it, how gameable it is, and who leans on it. SHARED with Model Radar — one canonical node per benchmark_slug; Harness Radar cites it via informs edges from harness dossiers and stamps type_data.radar_scope to include 'harness'. Identical section shape to Model Radar's benchmark_dossier so the two radars share one benchmark spine.

benchmark_slug.description: Canonical benchmark slug, lowercase-hyphenated (e.g. 'swe-bench-verified', 'terminal-bench', 'aider-polyglot'). This is the dossier's identity key.

last_synthesized_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of the most recent synthesis run that produced/updated this dossier.

measures.description: What the benchmark actually tests — task format, domain, scoring method — stated plainly enough to judge whether a score transfers to real work. For harness benchmarks, be explicit about the scaffold/agent-vs-model confound.

credibility_critique.description: Known critiques of the benchmark's validity: contamination, saturation, weak/wrong tests, harness sensitivity, construct-validity gaps. Each entry is a claim with stance, confidence, and sources.

gameability.description: How the benchmark can be (or has been) gamed: training on test data, scaffold/harness tuning, cherry-picked subsets, leaderboard overfitting, solution leakage. Each entry is a claim with stance, confidence, and sources.

cited_by.description: Who cites this benchmark and in what capacity, with source attribution — the trail of makers, evaluators, and practitioners leaning on it.

who.description: Named actor citing the benchmark (e.g. 'All Hands AI', 'OpenAI', 'Aider').

stance.description: The citing actor's stance (a maker citing it in a launch post = maker_claim).

context.description: How/why they cite it (e.g. 'headline metric in the OpenHands release').

popularity.description: How widely the benchmark is cited across the harvested corpus right now. 'high' = a headline metric makers lead with; 'medium' = regularly referenced; 'low' = niche/emerging or fading. Justify via cited_by and credibility_critique entries rather than extra fields.

score_context.description: OPTIONAL. Standings + dynamics derived from the append-only score_snapshots series stored in the benchmark package's type_data (for harness benchmarks, standings list harnesses).
